For a ring map <MATH_0001> let us define

We claim that <MATH_0004> is a local property of ring maps.
We check conditions (a), (b) and (c) of Definition
<REF_0001>. In the proof of
Lemma <REF_0002>
we have seen that (a), (b) and (c) hold for the property
of being ``of finite type''. Note that, for a finite type ring map

depends only on the local ring <MATH_0008> as an
algebra over <MATH_0009> where <MATH_0010>

For example, suppose <MATH_0011> is a ring map
such that all of the ring maps <MATH_0012> are quasi-finite
for <MATH_0013> generating the unit ideal.
We conclude that <MATH_0014> is of finite type. Also, for any
prime <MATH_0015> the local ring <MATH_0016>
is isomorphic as an <MATH_0017>-algebra to the local ring
<MATH_0018> for some <MATH_0019> and some
<MATH_0020>. Hence we conclude that
<MATH_0021> is quasi-finite at <MATH_0022>.
